{{short description|Arab biochemist}}
'''Usama Al-Khalidi''' ({{Langx|ar|أسامة الخالدي}}; April 20, 1932 – November 11, 2010) was an Arab biochemist who contributed significantly to the development of scientific institutions in [[Jordan]] and the wider [[Middle East and North Africa|Middle East]].

== Family and early life ==
Al-Khalidi was born in Jerusalem on April 20, 1932.<ref name=":0">"[https://static1.squarespace.com/static/551fa80de4b098a11a81f056/t/557736ffe4b0dc3248b5883b/1433876223134/Khalidi+Celebration+Booklet.pdf 2010. The Usama Al-Khalidi Scientific Day: Celebrating the life and scientific work of Professor Usama al-Khalidi]" (Event booklet). 2010. Middle East Medical Association, Beirut Lebanon.</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Biography|url=http://usama-alkhalidi.squarespace.com/bio|access-date=2020-11-15|website=Usama al-Khalidi|language=en-US}}</ref> His mother was Lebanese feminist writer [[Anbara Salam Khalidi]] (1897–1986), and his father was Palestinian educator [[Ahmad Samih Al Khalidi]] (1896-1951).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ahmad Samih al-Khalidi (1896 - 1951)|url=https://www.paljourneys.org/en/biography/9833/ahmad-samih-al-khalidi?fbclid=IwAR0tHsI3oiJJZL1WUlJ0TqHsnRwT0dHYrSpWZMr2EJSGm-goZmkAxay4BU0|access-date=2020-11-15|website=palestinian journeys|language=en|archive-date=2020-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116224036/https://www.paljourneys.org/en/biography/9833/ahmad-samih-al-khalidi?fbclid=IwAR0tHsI3oiJJZL1WUlJ0TqHsnRwT0dHYrSpWZMr2EJSGm-goZmkAxay4BU0|url-status=dead}}</ref> Usama was not the only child to go on to academic pursuits: his half-brother [[Walid Khalidi]] and brother [[Tarif Khalidi]] are both Palestinian historians. He also had two sisters, Randa and Karma.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ahmad Samih al-Khalidi (1896 - 1951)|url=https://www.paljourneys.org/en/biography/9833/ahmad-samih-al-khalidi?fbclid=IwAR0tHsI3oiJJZL1WUlJ0TqHsnRwT0dHYrSpWZMr2EJSGm-goZmkAxay4BU0|access-date=2020-11-15|website=palestinian journeys|language=en|archive-date=2020-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116224036/https://www.paljourneys.org/en/biography/9833/ahmad-samih-al-khalidi?fbclid=IwAR0tHsI3oiJJZL1WUlJ0TqHsnRwT0dHYrSpWZMr2EJSGm-goZmkAxay4BU0|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Anbara Salam Khalidi (1897 - 1986)|url=https://www.paljourneys.org/en/biography/9714/anbara-salam-khalidi|access-date=2020-11-15|website=palestinian journeys|language=en|archive-date=2019-11-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191107230931/https://www.paljourneys.org/en/biography/9714/anbara-salam-khalidi|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

== Early career: American University of Beirut ==
Al-Khalidi obtained his bachelor's and master's of science from the [[American University of Beirut]] (AUB) and his Ph.D. from the [[University of Michigan]]. He then returned to teach at AUB, serving as professor and chairman of the Biochemistry Department.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|date=Summer–Fall 2017|title=Our Legacy|url=https://www.aub.edu.lb/maingate/Documents/summer-fall-17.pdf|journal=American University of Beirut Magazine|volume=XVI|issue=1|pages=66–67}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Al-Khalidi|first=Usama|date=1972-10-01|title=Research at the Department of Biochemistry, American University of Beirut|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016%2F0020-711X%2872%2990001-8|journal=International Journal of Biochemistry|language=en|volume=3|issue=17|pages=491–497|doi=10.1016/0020-711X(72)90001-8|issn=0020-711X|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> His research during this period covered such topics as [[medical biochemistry]], animal tissue [[metabolism]], microbial biosynthesis, and metabolism of simple compounds.<ref name=":3" /> Specifically, he researched [[riboflavin]] biosynthesis, [[acetoin]] metabolism in mammals, [[Acetyl-CoA|acetyl-coA]] metabolism in liver supernatant, brain metabolism of [[acetoacetate]] and [[glucose]], and [[serum guanase]]. He published extensively on these topics in the 1960s and 70s. <ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shamma'a|first1=Munir H.|last2=Nasrallah|first2=Salah|last3=Chaglassian|first3=Toros|last4=Kachadurian|first4=Avedis K.|last5=al-Khalidi|first5=Usama A. S.|date=1965-02-01|title=Serum Xanthine Oxidase: A Sensitive Test of Acute Liver Injury|url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S001650856580141X|journal=Gastroenterology|language=en|volume=48|issue=2|pages=226–230|doi=10.1016/S0016-5085(65)80141-X|issn=0016-5085|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mudawwar|first1=Fuad|last2=Jebara|first2=Haifa|last3=Geha|first3=Raif|last4=al-Khalidi|first4=Usama|date=1976-03-01|title=A sensitive radiochemical assay for adenosine deaminase|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016%2F0090-1229%2876%2990022-2|journal=Clinical Immunology and Immunopathology|language=en|volume=5|issue=2|pages=173–176|doi=10.1016/0090-1229(76)90022-2|pmid=1277586|issn=0090-1229|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hajj|first1=S.|last2=Nasrallah|first2=S. Overall, al-Khalidi was part of an era of great change for the AUB Biochemistry Department, which only began awarding doctoral degrees in 1966.<ref name=":3" /> This was among the first doctoral programs at the university.<ref name=":2" />

== Later career ==
Al-Khalidi was a polymath. His interests also included medical and regional history, such as can be seen in his 1997 co-authorship of "Medical records, patients outcome, and peer review in eleventh-century Arab medicine" with [[Kamel Ajlouni|Kamel M. Ajlouni]] for the [[Annals of Saudi Medicine]]. In 1999, al-Khalidi was among the founding members of the [[Jordanian Society for Scientific Research, Entrepreneurship, and Creativity]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The founders {{!}} Jordan Society for Scientific Research - JSSR|url=https://jssr.jo/en/the-founders/|access-date=2020-11-15|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Honors ==
The [[Middle East Medical Association]] held an "Usama al-Khalidi Celebration Day" on April 24, 2010 in Beirut, just a few months prior to his passing.<ref name=":0" /> The [https://www.newton-gcrf.org/impact/where-we-work/jordan/ Newton-Khalidi Fund] of the UK Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy (BEIS) in Jordan is named in his honor in 2017 during the [[World Science Forum]] in Dead Sea, Jordan.<ref>{{Cite web|first=|date=2017-08-16|title=Agreement signed to establish Newton-Khalidi Fund|url=https://www.jordantimes.com/news/local/agreement-signed-establish-newton-khalidi-fund|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-12-03|website=Jordan Times|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=The Higher Council for Science and Technology|date=2020-03-04|title=Celebration of the Achievements of the Newton-Khalidi Fund in Promoting International Research Collaboration|url=http://www.hcst.gov.jo/en/node/1046|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-11-15|website=www.hcst.gov.jo|language=en}}</ref> In 2015, the Usama al-Khalidi Endowed Award was established at the American University of Beirut, to be given to an outstanding senior majoring in biology.<ref name=":2" />
